$comment: UX-14 (#137): the V2 performance budget, measured by .github/workflows/performance-budget.yml with Lighthouse CI on a production build; tools/performance-budget.mjs turns this file into the Lighthouse CI config and the run summary. Every value is the median of the runs. Sizes are compressed transfer sizes in KiB (1,024 bytes), as Lighthouse reports them, response headers included (next start serves HTTP/1.1, so each response carries its security headers uncompressed); times are milliseconds. `budget` is enforced: the measured median plus a margin (about 5 % on bytes, 2 requests, 6,000 ms of LCP, about 20 % above the medians measured (4.5 to 5.0 s): Lighthouse's simulated LCP moved by up to 12 % from run to run, so LCP is a backstop and the byte budgets are the precise guard, and 300 ms of TBT, 500 ms with the map, because CI runners vary most there), so a regression fails the check. `target` is where each screen should get to (the issue's targets and Lighthouse's 'good' thresholds); it is reported, not enforced, until the screen meets it.

screens.$comment: requests 44 -> 45 (#242, landing overview #133). The page's byte weight is unchanged: one stylesheet split in two. Next's CSS chunking (loose mode) merges modules greedily, in order of their positions across every route. The overview at /v2/landing adds another route that loads the @logloads/ui primitives, and InterestForm.module.css (4.7 KB, the job page's interest sheet) now gets its own file instead of joining the primitives' file (18.4 KB). Before, the two were one 23.1 KB file. Same bytes, one more request. Stopping it would take a cssChunking change in next.config.ts or dropping the primitives barrel from the overview. requests 45 -> 46 (#279, design audit 1 C1): app/v2/error.tsx, the V2 error boundary, is a client component, so Next loads its own chunk on every V2 route. Script requests 21 -> 22, script 260.4 -> 266.4 KiB (still under 270); stylesheets unchanged. Any segment error boundary costs this one request.
